title: CHILmesh: a fast 2D mesh library for triangular, quadrilateral, and mixed-element grids

creators.name: Kubatko, Ethan J.
creators.affiliation: Computational Hydrodynamics & Informatics Laboratory, The Ohio State University

description:
CHILmesh is a Python toolkit for two-dimensional triangular, quadrilateral and mixed-element meshes, designed so the meshes it builds and edits can be used by hydrodynamic models such as ADCIRC. It reads and writes ADCIRC mesh, forcing and output files, SMS .2dm and Gmsh files, peels a mesh into element layers from the boundary inward, smooths nodes with FEM, angle-based and truss smoothers, and reports element quality. The layer method follows the QuADMESH+ thesis (Mattioli, 2017). An optional prebuilt C++ backend runs full initialization 8.6 to 14.7 times faster than pure Python. Install with pip install chilmesh (pip install "chilmesh[cpp]" for the C++ backend); the import name is chilmesh.

This release (1.6.0)

Added

  • ADCIRC output readers: read_adcirc_output for ASCII fort.61 to fort.64, maxele.63 and maxvel.63 (full and sparse forms, single time-step seek, -99999 read as NaN), and read_adcirc_output_nc for the NetCDF forms (optional chilmesh[netcdf] extra) (#289).
  • ADCIRC forcing files: read_fort22_besttrack/write_fort22_besttrack for NOAA best-track storms, read_owi/write_owi for OWI wind and pressure, and readers and writers for fort.19, fort.20 and fort.24 boundary and tidal input.
  • CHILmesh.write_to_2dm: public SMS .2dm writer with boundary nodestrings; read_from_2dm reads them back.
  • color_elements: groups elements so that no two in a group share a node, for race-free parallel element loops.
  • partition_mesh and partition_report: spectral element partitioning (METIS through the optional chilmesh[partition] extra) with size, imbalance, cut-edge and connectivity reports.
  • chilplotting.plot_field: draws a nodal result on the mesh.
  • From 1.5.5: chilmesh.registry, a standard-library client for the Valence mesh registry; every download is checked against its SHA-256 hash.

Fixed

  • From 1.5.5: read_from_fort14 raises ValueError on a node id of 0 or above the node count (#282).

Roadmap at 1.6.0

  • Now: dropping Python 3.10 (end of life October 2026); the next release requires Python 3.11+. A native .chil container format (#201); ADCIRC hot-start files and byte-preserving fort.15 edits (#289).
  • Next: MCP server tools (#286); a streaming GPU mesh view (#167); a full-lifecycle benchmark on the STOFS-2D-Global mesh (#276).
  • Later: one ecosystem with ADMESH and QuADMESH.
